Hopkins (Belize)

Also find this entry through: Hopkins

Hopkins is a coastal village with a specifically documented Garifuna community context. These starting sources bring together a local drumming center’s voice, dated language fieldwork and a participatory tourism plan; each presents a particular view of village life.

Read the sources [1] Lebeha Drummers / Lebeha Drumming Center [2] University of Pennsylvania, ScholarlyCommons

Names & relationshipsA separately findable local village reading route for the Garifuna community context of Hopkins, Belize. The place includes a wider local population; this is not a claim that every resident is Garifuna or that this is a separate Indigenous nation or government.

01

Begin with a local cultural center

Lebeha’s own public account places the Center in northern Hopkins. It names Jabbar Lambey and Dorothy Pettersen as founders in 2002 and describes giving local children opportunities to learn music, dance and heritage. This is the Center’s account of its work, not a description of every family or a measured programme outcome.

Read the sources [1] Lebeha Drummers / Lebeha Drumming Center

02

A dated study of multilingual life

Maya Ravindranath’s 2009 dissertation draws on fieldwork in 2007–08, including interviews and work with a local consultant. It treats Garifuna, Belizean Creole and English as part of Hopkins’s changing social setting. Its observations are a historical snapshot; they do not establish current language ability, and speaking a language is not a test of someone’s identity.

Read the sources [2] University of Pennsylvania, ScholarlyCommons

03

Connections beyond the village

The same study describes how Hopkins residents combined local livelihoods with ties to Dangriga, other parts of Belize and relatives abroad. Schooling, work and remittances help readers see the village within wider networks. Those dated descriptions should be compared with later local accounts rather than treated as today’s economic census.

Read the sources [2] University of Pennsylvania, ScholarlyCommons

04

Reading a tourism plan as a plan

The January 2019 destination plan records a stakeholder vision that includes Garifuna and other cultural experiences. It emphasizes community participation, local businesses and training, while noting concerns over who benefits from tourism. These are planning priorities and reported concerns, not proof that the proposed benefits reached everyone.

Read the sources [3] Belize Tourism Board; prepared by Praxi5 Advisory Group Ltd.

Lebeha Drumming Center — its own public account ↗

The Center’s own substantive account identifies its Hopkins setting, names founders Jabbar Lambey and Dorothy Pettersen, dates its beginning to 2002 and describes opportunities for local children to learn drumming, dance and heritage.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual complete LEBEHA DRUMMING CENTER body and 2005 teacher/group caption retrieved normally HTTP 200 and read. Not merely the website navigation; linked albums, music, videos and booking/contact material not reviewed.

Review recorded: October 29, 2026

Access note: Undated current webpage with dated retrospective claims. A self-description, not independent programme evaluation, evidence of all village practices or a present schedule. No photographs/music reproduced or rights inferred from the account.

https://lebeha.com/
Contemporary life·Music·Education·Community history
Academic / sociolinguistic dissertationUniversity of Pennsylvania, ScholarlyCommonsSource 2

Language Shift and the Speech Community: Sociolinguistic Change in a Garifuna Community in Belize ↗

Publication: 2009

Maya Ravindranath’s 2009 dissertation offers a dated study of multilingual Hopkins and a comparative teacher survey in four villages. Read the selected fieldwork and methods pages alongside community accounts; language use does not determine identity.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual primary university record and linked 217-page PDF retrieved HTTP 200. Read printed pp.20–29 and31–32 (PDFpp.31–40,42–43) for Hopkins/site/methods, and printed pp.124–126 (PDFpp.135–137) for teacher-survey methods and interpretation. Not the full dissertation.

Review recorded: October 29, 2026

Access note: A 2007–08 fieldwork snapshot, published 2009. No present speaker totals, language-disappearance claim, proficiency ranking, census or universal ethnicity inference. Figures, complete linguistic analyses, interviews themselves and underlying works not independently inspected. Private family recordings not reproduced.

https://repository.upenn.edu/items/a26ec281-1dce-4683-811e-c32e000e2bfc

Hopkins Tourism Destination Development Plan ↗

Publication: January 2019

A January 2019 planning document records a stakeholder vision combining Garifuna and other cultural experiences with local participation, entrepreneurship and training. Use it to examine goals and anticipated tensions, not as proof of later delivery.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual 128-page PDF retrieved normally HTTP 200. Cover/contents and selected Executive Summary PDFpp.9–12 read; the opening Executive Summary page was independently reopened for its stakeholder-vision and community-participation body.

Review recorded: October 29, 2026

Access note: Not all128pages, appendices, mapped areas, statistics, legal framework or later implementation inspected. Tourism forecasts/current totals and completed economic outcomes are not adopted. Photographs/maps not reproduced.

https://belizetourismboard.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Hopkins-TDDP-Final-.pdf
